Bug_Details:
StringBuilder does not have a char constructor; this invokes the int constructor. StringBuilder does not have a char constructor, so instead this code creates a
StringBuilder with initial size equal to the code point of the specified char.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by initializing a StringBuilder with a char value. Instead of appending the character 'A' to the StringBuilder, it initializes the StringBuilder with an initial capacity equal to the ASCII value of 'A', which is 65.
Trigger_Explanation: The test triggers the bug by calling the showBug method with the character 'A'. The StringBuilder is initialized with the integer value of 'A' (which is 65), instead of the character itself. This results in a StringBuilder with an initial capacity of 65 and no characters appended initially. When 'Hello' is appended, the final string is just 'Hello', not 'AHello' as expected.
